record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of microwave heating
record.context_brief: Global existence under the integral condition on q
record.original_question: For the full nonlinear microwave-heating problem coupling Maxwell's equations with the heat equation, is the integral condition ∫_0^∞ dξ/q(ξ) = ∞ sufficient to guarantee that the solution exists for all time t ∈ [0,∞)?

evidence.quote: An additional difficulty is to establish under what assumptions this solution is defined in [0, ∞).
Remark In view of the above considerations it appears not unreasonable to presume that ∫_0^∞ 1/q(ξ) dξ = ∞ is the key assumption to prove that problem (1)–(9) has a solution defined in [0, ∞).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the full nonlinear microwave-heating problem in which the time-harmonic Maxwell system for the electromagnetic field is coupled to the heat equation for the temperature u(x,t) in a bounded domain Ω ⊂ R^3 (with appropriate initial and boundary conditions on the electromagnetic field and on u). The coupling enters through a temperature-dependent electrical conductivity and through the volumetric heat-absorption rate q(u) ≥ 0, where q : [0,∞) → (0,∞) is a given continuous, nondecreasing function. The temperature evolution takes the schematic form
   u_t − Δu = q(u) |E|^2,
together with Maxwell's equations whose coefficients depend on u via q (and the conductivity).

Question: Is the integral condition
   ∫_0^∞ dξ / q(ξ) = ∞
sufficient to ensure that, for every admissible set of initial-boundary data, the coupled Maxwell–heat system admits a solution defined for all t ∈ [0, ∞) (i.e., no finite-time blow-up of the temperature occurs)?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that the Osgood-type integral condition ∫_0^∞ dξ/q(ξ) = ∞ suffices for global-in-time existence of the full nonlinear Maxwell–heat microwave-heating system appears to remain open. Existing global existence results address either bounded conductivity, one-dimensional reductions, or polynomial growth conditions q(u) ~ u^q with restricted exponents, rather than establishing the general Osgood-type criterion for the full 3D coupled problem.

status_evidence.title: Regularity of weak solution to Maxwell's equations and applications to microwave heating
status_evidence.snippet: Regularity and existence results for Maxwell's equations coupled to a nonlinear heat equation modeling microwave heating.
status_evidence.claim: Global existence is established under restrictive conditions (bounded conductivity, or special geometric/dimensional reductions), not under a general Osgood-type integral condition on q.

status_evidence.title: Existence of solutions for the problem of microwave heating and a Liapunoff criteria for stability and instability
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of solutions for the microwave heating problem with stability criteria.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to study existence under specific structural assumptions, indicating the general Osgood-type criterion remains a conjecture.

status_evidence.title: On Maxwell's Equations with a Temperature Effect, II
status_evidence.snippet: Global smooth solutions in one dimension when σ(u) ~ u^q with growth restrictions.
status_evidence.claim: Global existence for the full coupled system is known only under growth or dimensional restrictions stronger than the Osgood integral condition.
